title: Proteomic characterization of adipose tissue from cold-exposed mice
projectDescription: Cold stimulation not only activates the thermogenesis activity of brown adipose tissue (BAT) but also induces browning of white adipose tissue (WAT). To elucidate the mechanisms underlying cold-induced thermogenesis and adipose tissue remodeling, we used RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) and liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) to examine the transcriptomic and proteomic profiles, respectively, of adipose tissue from mice exposed to cold or thermoneutral temperature. The male C57BL/6J mice were divided into three groups (5 mice/group), two groups were kept at 6 ˚C for 6 h and 24 h, respectively, and the control group were kept at 22 ˚C for 24 h. Subsequently, the BAT and inguinal WAT of each mouse were dissected and subjected to RNA-seq and data-independent acquisition (DIA)-based LC-MS/MS.
sampleProcessingProtocol: C57BL/6J mice were obtained from Hunan Slac Jingda Laboratory Company (Changsha, China). Male mice aged 7-8 weeks were housed in a chamber with controlled light/dark cycle (12/12 h) and controlled temperature (22˚C) before cold exposure. Water and food were provided ad libitum. For cold exposure, mice were divided into three groups (5 mice/group). Two groups were kept at 6 ˚C for 6 h and 24 h, respectively, and the control mice were kept at 22 ˚C for 24 h. After cold exposure, the mice were euthanized by cervical dislocation and then the BAT and inguinal WAT (iWAT) were dissected.Adipose tissue was homogenized in SDT lysis buffer (4% SDS, 100 mM DTT, 100 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0), then boiled for 3 min followed by ultrasonication at 4 ˚C for 2 min. After centrifugation at 16,000 g for 20 min, the supernatant was collected and the protein concentration in the supernatant was determined by bicinchoninic acid assay (Beyotime Biotechnology, Shanghai, China). Proteins were digested with trypsin (Promega) at a ratio of 50: 1 overnight at 37 ˚C according to the FASP method described by Wisniewski et al11. The peptide mixtures were collected by centrifugation (16 000 g, 15 min), desalted with C18 StageTip (Thermo Scientific) for further LC-MS analysis and dried in a vacuum dryer. The peptides were redissolved in buffer A (0.1% formic acid in water) prior to LC–MS/MS.
dataProcessingProtocol: The DIA-NN software (version 1.8.1) was used for the database search and the quantitative analysis of the MS. The database is the UniProtKB (10090-87491-20241204.fasta, downloaded on 04.12.2024) (https://www.uniprot.org/taxonomy/10090). The parameters for the database search were set as follows: digestion enzyme: trypsin, max missed cleavages: 1, fixed modifications: carbamidomethylation of cysteine, variable modifications: acetylation of N-terminal and oxidation of methionine, peptide length range: 7-30, charge of peptide: 1- 4, fragment ion m/z range: 150-2000. Database search results were filtered and exported with a false discovery rate (FDR) of <1%.
